knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: The fourth case involved a five-month-old female infant who was brought to our clinic due to failure to thrive and inadequate weight gain. During the physical examination, the findings included a normal first heart sound (S1), a fixed splitting of the second heart sound (S2), and a grade 2/6 systolic murmur located at the left sternal border.. Confirmed diagnosis: Pulmonary Hypertension associated with Atrial Septal Defect. Differential diagnosis includes: Pulmonary Hypertension associated with Atrial Septal Defect.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Pulmonary Hypertension associated with Atrial Septal Defect

knowledge_fragments.content: In summary, the homozygous missense variant p.(Arg367Trp) causes a clinically consistent, multisystem disease with mildly delayed motor and severely impaired speech development, microcephaly, failure to thrive, short statue, muscular hypotonia, ataxia, brain atrophy, microcytic anemia, hepatomegaly, hypothyroidism, and facial features including a deep set eyes, a flat philtrum, and open mouth appearance. Clinical heterogeneity is only observed for hypothyroidism (approximately 50% of patients affected) and some sporadic findings such as hearing loss or gastroesophageal reflux.
knowledge_fragments.title: The recurrent missense mutation p.(Arg367Trp) in YARS1 causes a distinct neurodevelopmental phenotype. > Results > Homozygous YARS1 c.1099C > T, p.(Arg367Trp) variant causes a distinct multisystem disease

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A three-month-old male infant presented with stridor and failure to thrive. He was delivered vaginally at full-term with a birth weight of 3.5 kg and had an uncomplicated neonatal course. His parents reported noisy and difficult breathing a few days after birth, which progressively worsened and was associated with episodes of cyanosis and poor bottle feeding. At one month of age, a general pediatrician noted stridor and poor weight gain and advised increasing the frequency of feeds. The parents sought medical advice multiple times, including emergency department visits for significant respiratory distress, increasing stridor, and failure to thrive. He was referred to our neurology clinic for assessment of hypotonia. No workup was performed, and he was not hospitalized before the referral. Physical examination revealed inspiratory stridor, suprasternal and subcostal retractions, tachypnea, and bilaterally reduced air entry. His oxygen saturation was 93% in room air and improved slightly with oxygen supplementation. His weight at presentation was 4.2 kg, below the 3rd percentile of the WHO growth chart. No dysmorphic features were observed. Chest X-ray and routine labor

knowledge_fragments.content: In a reported case, RO occurred in a child who showed translocation between chromosomes 13 and 10, in addition to a central nervous system midline defect. In almost all cases, hyponatremia was persistent despite sodium administration and treatment with hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. One more case was described in the infantile period, in a 6-month-old infant who showed failure to thrive as a unique symptom.

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: Patient IV-1: A 14-year-old female was first evaluated at the age of three years for global developmental delay, short stature, and failure to thrive. She was born at 39 weeks of gestation, weighing 3.8 kg, with no complications at birth. Developmental concerns were observed after six months, including developmental issues associated with poor feeding and failure to thrive. No facial dysmorphic features were noted. Seizures and retinal degeneration were identified during the first two years of life.. Confirmed diagnosis: Salt and Pepper Syndrome. Differential diagnosis includes: Salt and Pepper Syndrome.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Salt and Pepper Syndrome

knowledge_fragments.content: A careful physical examination is as important as a careful history. Examination is usually normal, however atypical signs and symptoms need to be identified to think of alternative possible diseases. The diagnosis of asthma should be reconsidered in case of the following: (1) presence of clubbing, cyanosis, significant anemia or nasal polyps; (2) failure to thrive.

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: [Splenomegaly and failure to thrive as a result of Gaucher disease].. Salient findings: involvement of the bones, bone marrow and spleen or liver; massive splenomegaly; poor growth; learning difficulties; extreme fatigue for several years. Confirmed diagnosis: Gaucher disease (GD). Differential diagnosis includes: Gaucher disease (GD); lysosomal storage disease; GD.

knowledge_fragments.content:
A wide variety of infections should be considered in neonates who are ill, febrile, or hypothermic.

Infections such as congenital rubella, syphilis, toxoplasmosis, and CMV should be considered, particularly

in neonates with abnormalities such as growth restriction, deafness, microcephaly, anomalies, failure to

thrive, hepatosplenomegaly, or neurologic abnormalities.
knowledge_fragments.title: Chapter 279. Infections in Neonates > Infections in Neonates > Diagnosis

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A Saudi Infant with Vici Syndrome: Case Report and Literature Review.. Salient findings: agenesis of the corpus callosum; hypopigmentation; cardiomyopathy; progressive failure to thrive; dysmorphic features; immunodeficiency; cataracts; recurrent chest infection; psychomotor delay; chest infection; significant left ventricular dilation with a Z-score of 3.1; moderate mitral and tricuspid regurgitation; depressed ventricular function with a fractional shortening of 17% and ejection fraction 37%; died; extensive system involvement; death; rapid deterioration; improve life expectancy. Confirmed diagnosis: Vici syndrome. Differential diagnosis includes: Vici syndrome.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Vici syndrome

knowledge_fragments.content:
The clinical presentation of neonatal TB is nonspecific but is usually marked by multiple organ

involvement. The neonate may look acutely or chronically ill and may have fever, lethargy, respiratory

distress, hepatosplenomegaly, or failure to thrive.
